review.reviewer: independent PH-264 membership-lifecycle reviewer (fresh context, read-only)
findings: SERVICE CORRECTNESS VERIFIED: change_membership takes the company lock, re-reads the operator as an active owner, validates role in {owner,pm,finance,member,auditor}, validates project_scope as a list of unique same-org project ids, enforces expected_version when supplied, rejects writes to an inactive target unless it is a restore, and rejects company-level roles (owner/finance/auditor) carrying a non-empty scope. Project scope is maintained as a ProjectMember diff; deactivation requires no active Employee binding and no active (not closed/cancelled) project manager, cannot self-deactivate, and the last active owner cannot be demoted/deactivated. Deactivation updates role/active/version and, in the same transaction, revokes all unrevoked AgentToken rows, clears all ProjectMember rows and writes one generic audit; restore increments version and does not restore old scope or tokens. Tests cover golden role/scope changes, scope diff/rejections, employee/manager handoff, restore, last-owner/self rules, non-owner denial, expected-version/replay, dry-run zero side effects, cross-org denial and snapshot read permissions.

IDEMPOTENCY/AUDIT ACCEPTED AS DISCLOSED: the task reuses the append-only AuditEvent payload (action identity.membership.changed with request_token/input_digest/result) rather than adding a new receipt table, because the frozen spec allows only the Membership.version column as a structural change. Same token+same input returns the stored result, changed input conflicts, and dry_run returns a preview without writes/audit. The audit payload contains changed_fields/role/active/project_scope_ids/revoked_token_count/request_token/digest/result and no password/token hash/email; the generic audit helper's ordinary non-canonical outbox DomainEvent is disclosed and no canonical identity event topic is added. This is an acceptable implementation choice for the frozen scope, with the limitation documented in report.deviations.

MIGRATION/MODEL/BOUNDARY: core 0010 is a single AddField Membership.version (PositiveIntegerField default 1, dependency core 0009), no trigger, no applied-migration rewrite, no PK/account clone, no new business table, no ledger/amount/period writes; Settings UI only extends the existing settings page/form and does not add a route, while the membership service remains owner-write with finance/auditor read and pm/member self-only snapshot (HTTP tests cover owner/finance visibility, pm 403, non-owner write 403 and deactivated-member denial). The disclosed integer-PK and manager 'active project' stage interpretation are reasonable; a browser 1440/390 run is still outstanding (HTTP tests only).

Code review confirms company-locked/fresh owner-only change_membership with expected-version, role/company-scope rules, ProjectMember diff, last-owner/self-deactivate/employee-binding/manager-handoff guards, same-transaction AgentToken revocation and scope clearing, restore without scope/token revival, version increment, audit-without-sensitive-fields, idempotent audit-payload replay (disclosed receipt-table substitute), single AddField core migration, settings-only UI without new route, and owner-write/finance-auditor-read/pm-member-self service permissions. deviations: Idempotency reuses the append-only AuditEvent payload (action identity.membership.changed, payload.request_token + input_digest + result) instead of adding a receipt table, because the frozen PH-264 spec forbids new business tables and allows only Membership.version as the structural change. Same token+input replays the stored result; changed input conflicts.

The generic audit helper also emits its ordinary non-canonical outbox DomainEvent for the action name; no canonical event topic is added to the contract catalog and no canonical event id is claimed by the command result. Report discloses this generic outbox row.
Active project for the manager-handoff guard means a Project whose stage is not closed/cancelled; the spec says 'active 项目的 manager' without enumerating stages, so this interpretation is disclosed.

core.Membership and core.Project use integer primary keys; the service accepts integer ids (and numeric strings) and returns ids as strings, while the canonical command payload schema is followed semantically. No cloned account or UUID PK change was made.

Single worker owns the whole write set for this task (core/models.py Membership.version, core/masterdata.py service, core/forms.py form, core/views.py settings handler, core/migrations/0010, templates/settings.html, tests, governance); no parallel slice writes these files; independent review is pending.
project/manifest.json active_handoff is left at main's value per the integration convention; tasks.json records PH-264 in_review with owner/handoff.
No browser 1440/390 check was run in this round (HTTP tests only); no new canonical event topic, ledger/amount/period write or AgentToken capability was added.

CI fix after the first PostgreSQL run: the preparation multi-connection probe inserts core_membership rows with raw SQL (no version column), so the module-level default=1 alone left PostgreSQL with no column default and the insert failed with NotNullViolation. Membership.version now also declares db_default=1 (migration 0010 emits DEFAULT 1), which keeps the preparation contract valid; SQLite scoped tests re-ran OK (17 tests) and the PostgreSQL rerun is the authoritative evidence.
